articles.title: How WinHelp files work
articles.summary: WinHelp files are a complex archive format that uses a combination of LZ77 compression and a B+ tree index to store and retrieve their contents. This format allows developers to read and write WinHelp files, which are used to manage and customize Microsoft Office applications. The key to understanding WinHelp files is to grasp their internal structure, which consists of a file system that starts with a magic number followed by the position of an internal directory, and a B+ tree index that stores the contents of the directory. This format is particularly useful for developers who need to work with old WinHelp files or create new ones.
